review_output: {"summary":"The prior MAJOR (unmeasured scale bound) is largely addressed for the pure helper. The 8192-bit cap bounds BigInt width, the near-cap disjoint-segment benchmark is independently oracle-checked, and the historical reference is hash-pinned and labeled. I found no new arithmetic defects: the sorted-start union, monotone predicate and early exit remain correct. What remains is representativeness and availability. The benchmark uses a 0..5600 ms wall range, about 13 binary-search iterations, where real epoch-scale windows need 25-53. The cohort budget and cohort-wide scale poisoning may leave the completion metrics unavailable at modest real volumes. The cap itself is not pinned at its boundary in the vitest suite. All of this is scoped to pure helpers, not API/DB/UI/WP acceptance.","findings":[{"severity":"MAJOR","area":"availability / scale contract","file":"src/lib/live-core-metrics-read-model.ts","issue":"The cohort-wide 10,000-segment budget counts every post-verification segment, including exact retransmission duplicates, and a single limit_exceeded (aggregate or one person's >8192-bit scale) makes completionRate and postCompletionOrderRate unavailable for the whole cohort. At the 5 s sample gap that playbackSegment allows, one hour of viewing is about 720 segments, so roughly 14 such viewers exhaust the budget. Any adapter that coalesces samples into long segments with arbitrary durations can hit the 8192-bit scale after a few hundred segments, because the cap is only guaranteed unreachable for durations <=5000 ms (lcm(1..5000) is about 2^7213).","evidence":"`completionLimit` is initialised from the total segment count across all people (> MAX_REPORT_COMPLETION_SEGMENTS). One person's `firstCompletionTime` limit_exceeded sets `completionLimit = true` for everyone. The tests only cover 10001 identical rows and 6000+6000 rows. Nothing shows a realistic cohort size staying available.","impact":"The fail-closed behavior is honest and not a correctness bug, but two of the five approved metrics may be permanently 'limit_exceeded' for ordinary live events. The performance fix then trades latency for availability.","recommended_fix":"Dedupe identical segments before budgeting. Prefer durable verified first-completion facts, with a sampled or audited reconciliation, over recomputing from raw segments for large cohorts. Define and document the supported cohort/segment envelope for the adapter, including coalescing rules that keep wall durations <=5000 ms or the lcm within the cap.","required_test":"Fixture of about 100 viewers x 720 segments (5 s samples) with the product-expected volume, asserting the intended result (available, or an explicitly specified limit) and a measured wall-time budget. Add a test that retransmitted duplicates do not consume budget.","confidence":0.6},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"benchmark representativeness / evidence reproducibility","file":"docs/ai-team/evidence/product-audit-20261011/WP-20/full-metrics/performance-check.mjs","issue":"The near-cap benchmark uses wallStart=0 and wall times <=5600 ms, so binary search runs only about 13 iterations. Real histories use epoch-scale timestamps, with a search range of min wallStart to max wallEnd that can span hours or days (about 24-30 iterations) and up to 53 iterations in the worst case. At about 30-40 ms per near-cap iteration, extrapolated cost is about 1-1.7 s on this machine, close to the 2 s budget. The measurement is also a single un-repeated run.","evidence":"The checked-in JSON shows 420 ms / 491 ms, while the review brief quotes 425 ms / 343 ms. That is up to 43% run-to-run variance for the same case. No machine or Node info is recorded. Each case is measured once, and the scale cases have wallStartMs=0 for all rows.","impact":"The '<2 s' claim may not hold for the true worst-case shape, and the receipt can't be reproduced to within a stable margin.","recommended_fix":"Add near-cap cases offset to epoch-scale wall times (for example +1.7e12 and a one-week spread, with the crossing near the end of the range). Report median and max of N>=5 runs plus Node version and CPU. Set the budget with explicit headroom, or lower the cap.","required_test":"Re-run the 1..5600 and 1..5000 scale cases with a wall-time base of 1.7e12 and a range of at least 6e8 ms, still checked by the directed-rounding oracle, with the median of 5 runs under budget.","confidence":0.55},{"severity":"MINOR","area":"regression coverage of the cap boundary","file":"src/lib/live-viewing-evidence.test.ts","issue":"The 8192-bit cap and its near-boundary behavior are exercised only by the out-of-suite .mjs script. The vitest suite pins only a far-over-cap case (1000 durations near 1e12). A change to MAX_RATIONAL_SCALE, to the scale-update order, or to the early-exit logic could silently make legitimate durations <=5000 return limit_exceeded, or let the cost grow, without failing CI.","evidence":"The only scale test in the unit tests is `bounds the common rational scale...`, with durations 1e12+i. There is no test with durations 1..5000 (expected available) or 1..~5700 (expected limit_exceeded).","impact":"The measured envelope is not protected by the automated tests, so regressions would be invisible.","recommended_fix":"Add unit tests asserting that wall durations 1..5000 (the maximum playbackSegment gap) always return available, and that a set exceeding lcm 2^8192 returns limit_exceeded. Optionally export or derive the cap and assert 2^7213 < cap.","required_test":"firstCompletionTime on 5000 disjoint segments with durations 1..5000 returns status 'available' with the oracle-verified time. A set of durations 1..5800 returns limit_exceeded.","confidence":0.6},{"severity":"NIT","area":"validation ordering under limit","file":"src/lib/live-core-metrics-read-model.ts","issue":"When completionLimit is set, orderMetrics copies the limit_exceeded result and returns before validating completions/orders and reconciling durable facts. Contradictory or malformed completion/order rows therefore surface as limit_exceeded rather than invalid_data, and provisionalConversions stays null. Because the structural validation is skipped, the reason alone can't distinguish bad data from load.","evidence":"orderMetrics starts with `if (result.completionRate.status === 'unavailable') { result.postCompletionOrderRate = { ...result.completionRate }; return; }`. This runs before the `requireFact` checks on input.completions/input.orders.","impact":"Low. Possibly masks upstream data-quality failures on exactly the large cohorts where they are hardest to notice.","recommended_fix":"Run the cheap structural validation of completions/orders (ids, timestamps, boolean cancelled, duplicate-conflict) before the limit early-return. Skip only the expensive derived reconciliation.","required_test":"With 10001 viewing rows plus a conflicting duplicate completion fact, expect postCompletionOrderRate invalid_data, and still limit_exceeded for clean facts.","confidence":0.45}]}
